item.title: [ 87] Elon Musk Melts Down Over Perfectly Normal Questions in Wild New Interview
item.description:
https://gizmodo.com/elon-musk-economist-interview-2000790016

Elon Musk sat down with the editor-in-chief of the Economist for a taped interview that went live Thursday. The Tesla CEO has been avoiding normal journalists recently, even cancelling a planned interview with CNBC earlier this month. And it now seems pretty obvious why. Musk has a hard time answering normal questions about his often fascist and sometimes incoherent worldview.

The interview started cordially enough, with Economist editor Zanny Minton Beddoes asking Musk about his thoughts on the future of artificial intelligence. Musk said many things that he’s said before, including that AI will deliver an age of abundance, where “anyone can have anything they think of.”

Musk insisted that AI will exceed human intelligence in five years and that humans will no longer be in charge of the world in 10 years. Beddoes pressed Musk several times on what that means and how his companies will continue to exist. The billionaire rambled on and on in a way that didn’t really stand up to any scrutiny.

“If you have vast numbers of robots with vast amounts of digital intelligence, you have a sort of a quasi-infinite economy,” said Musk. “The future is going to be very, very different from the past. There’s no analogy or metaphor that I think illustrates the magnitude of change that we’re going to experience here.”

item.title: [ 30] Earth is literally boring, where else can I go?
item.description:
I worked in finance and hit it big when I was 26, allowed me to become a full time investor and I spent the past 10 years travelling and enjoying my life.

You might not understand this because you're either too broke or young to travel, but literally every country fucking sucks now. I remember travelling with parents before the world became "internet-fied" and different places felt genuinely unique. But now? Everything has been commodified, everyone just wants money, everyone sees the latest trends on social media and deploys them locally for tourists.

It's really gay. 2017-2018 really were the last good years of travelling, mainly because social media hadn't rooted itself so deeply in every human being.

So I haven't been EVERYWHERE, only about 40 countries, and I mostly avoid black countries and have only lightly travelled India, but I'm looking for suggestions on whether there is anything actually interesting to see anymore. Not looking to do Europe because that's where I spent most of my time.

Sometimes there's actually good advice here among the drivel

item.title: [ 45] Why does America reward investors far more than it rewards workers? It's a w
item.description:
Why does America reward investors far more than it rewards workers?

It's a weird paradox because societies need lots of hard work in order to maintain themselves and all their system. Maintaining a system of laws and justice requires a lot of work. Maintaining a sewage system requires a lot of work. Maintaining ports and water ways requires a lot of work.

However, workers are the most abused and lowest paid group of Americans. In contrast, investors make money simply off owning things. You can literally buy stock and just do nothing but sit on your ass holding for 5 years and make a handsome profit.

The system we currently have does not incentivise work at all. Instead it incentives the lack of work because that yields the lowest reward.

> why no Taiwan general in the catalog edition, grok writing the OP edition

Quick Start Guide for First Timers:

Visa: Most countries get 90 days visa-free. Check if you need an eVisa or ARC if staying longer. Fill out your arrival card online before arriving for less stress.
Best Time: Oct–Dec for perfect weather (dry season). Avoid July–Sept typhoon season unless you like rain and chaos.
Getting Around: Taipei MRT is clean, cheap, and efficient as fuck. Youbike only needs an easy card and is essentially free unless you want to ride for hours.
High Speed Rail (HSR) for city hopping (Taipei Kaohsiung in ~1.5h).
Scooters are god outside Taipei. Get an international permit if you plan to ride.
Uber works but taxis are cheap. Avoid during rush hour or rain.

Food:

Night markets are mandatory. Shilin, Raohe, Ningxia, etc.
Must eats: Beef noodle soup, stinky tofu (acquired taste), oyster omelettes, bubble tea (original homeland), pineapple cake, mango shaved ice. All you can eat hotpot also.
7-11 and FamilyMart are better than in most countries, you can live off them if you want.

Top Spots:

Taipei: 101, Jiufen old street, Beitou hot springs, temples everywhere.
Taroko Gorge (east coast) — absolute kino nature.
Sun Moon Lake, Kenting (beaches), Alishan for mountains.
East coast for chill vibes and fewer tourists.

General Tips:

Taiwanese people are polite and helpful. Learn basic Mandarin or use Google Translate.
Tipping is not expected.

Useful Links & Services:

Official Taiwan Tourism: https://eng.taiwan.net.tw/
YouBike: https://en.youbike.com.tw/

item.title: [ 66] Herp Derp (herpetology appreciation)
item.description:
A thread for all them big beautiful amphibians and reptiles you’ve seen while /out/. Snakes, frogs, turtles, lizards, and toads.
I miss seeing frogs and toads. When I was a kid you could let ride your bike down the road without seeing dozens of pancaked toads on the road… it’s been decades since I’ve seen that now.
This big bastard casually strolled through my lawn one morning so I captured it and let it go at the lake. I do not need any snappers hanging around.

item.title: [ 82] Alone season 13
item.description:
Alone airs tonight, lets get the seasonal thread going as they are some of my favorite comfy threads.
This year its "Alone: World Championship"
This season, survivalists from seven different countries are represented including the United States x3 kek, Canada, Wales, Australia, Slovenia, Portugal, and New Zealand.

It is set within the Arctic Circle along the rugged Richardson Mountains in the Northwest Territories of Aklavik, about 150km from where they filmed Season 11
Hopefully its more interesting as I found the last few seasons lacking

item.title: [ 53] So I happened upon an ad for an "outdoors bidet", which screws onto your water
item.description:
So I happened upon an ad for an "outdoors bidet", which screws onto your water bottle and lets you wash your ass when you take a shit.
The woman said that it frees you from carrying your used toilet paper.
Herein comes the question, who the fuck carries his used TP?
You know you can just leave it in the wilderness and it will decompose, right?

item.title: [194] Backpacking kit & gear
item.description:
What does your backpacking kit look like & what are your favorite pieces of gear you have that are unusual or greatly increased your quality of life on the trail? This is my basic kit alot of the gear is 10 years old or more I have recently added a camp chair & a little bidet that goes on a water bottle. My favorite piece of gear is not pictures but it is a frybake pan which is basically a lightweight dutch oven I will be using it on my trip at the end of this month to roast a chicken & make stuffing.
